rules.title: Capabilities are reachable without the UI
rules.description: Every meaningful action is invokable without the user interface, through a capability, command, API, or tool an authorized agent can call.
rules.rationale: The UI must not be the only first-class client. Humans and agents operate the same underlying capabilities.
rules.remediation: Expose the underlying capability the UI calls, and have the UI call it too.

rules.title: Business logic does not depend on a specific AI provider
rules.description: Model providers sit behind an abstraction so capabilities remain stable when the model changes.
rules.rationale: A capability that breaks when the model changes was never a capability.
rules.remediation: Introduce a provider interface and move direct SDK calls behind it.

rules.title: Propose is separate from execute
rules.description: An agent can recommend a change without applying it.
rules.rationale: Separating recommendation from application is what makes agent work reviewable before it takes effect.
rules.remediation: Split the capability into a proposal that returns a plan and an execution that applies one.

rules.title: Destructive actions require explicit approval
rules.description: Destructive or high-impact actions require explicit approval unless the project's policy says otherwise.
rules.rationale: Irreversible action taken without approval cannot be undone by improving the process afterwards.
rules.remediation: Gate the action behind an approval step that records who approved it.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible: a project may declare this not-applicable when it has no destructive actions, but it may not waive approval while having them.
